Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html

## Changelog[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changelog)

All notable changes to PREFLIGHT are recorded here. Entries follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); released versions are Git tags.

### Unreleased[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

- Added: `scripts/a11y.sh --base-url` and `scripts/a11y.ps1 -BaseUrl` (or `A11Y_BASE_URL`) check a running site locally, as the component's `base_url` input does in CI.

### 0.2.0 (2026-11-07)[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-0-2026-11-07)

- Changed (breaking for 0.1.4 includes of `portability`): the `portability` component is one job that runs the six checks of ADR-0010 decision 5 instead of goss. It builds the image with Buildah (vfs storage, chroot isolation: no Docker daemon, no privileged runner, no registry push), boots it twice side by side as an arbitrary uid in group 0 with no capabilities and no passwd entry, and probes it with curl: the strict boot (app root not writable, writable paths writable by group 0, the port variable honored, no writes outside `writable_paths` and `runtime_paths`), then `health` (200 to `Host: 10.1.2.3:<port>`), `env-only` (no `.env` or config cache in the image), `forwarded-headers` (forged `X-Forwarded-*` and identity headers change nothing), `logs` (stdout or stderr, nothing under `logs_path`), `session-hop` (a sign-in survives a hop to the second replica) and `sigterm` (the main process handles SIGTERM and exits within `stop_timeout`). One `portability: <check>: pass|FAIL|skipped` line per check. The probe is `templates/portability/probe.sh`, inlined in the template byte for byte; new contract test `tests/check-portability-inline` (sh and ps1, with a write mode) keeps the two in step.
- Changed: `portability` inputs. `buildah_image` is renamed `image` (same default); the app-image `image` input is gone; `start_command` is optional (empty runs the image's `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`); new `job_name` (default `portability`), `build_args`, `runtime_paths`, `port_env`, `env`, `stop_timeout`, `probe_path`, `identity_header`, `session_login_path`, `session_check_path`, `logs_path` and `checks`. `contract/inputs.json` lists the new set and the one job; `tests/check-job-names` now covers `portability`, and `tests/check-image-inputs` has no exemptions left.
- Added: a must-fail proof for `portability`: one fixture app, `tests/portability/app`, built clean and once per flaw (`ARG FLAW`: needs-root, writes-root, fixed-port, host-bound, dotenv, trusts-proxy, file-logs, file-sessions, no-term-handler). `tests/check-portability` (sh, run inside the Buildah image, and a ps1 wrapper that runs it with Docker and `seccomp=unconfined`, never `--privileged`) passes only when the clean build passes and each flaw fails the check it targets. Preflight's pipeline includes the component on the clean fixture and runs the check as `must-fail-portability`.
- Removed: `templates/portability/goss.yaml`, the goss download, the registry push and the `tests/portability/good`, `bad-needs-root` and `bad-writes-root` fixtures.
- Changed: The canonical repository is git.wayne.edu (ADR-0021); docs, links and package metadata no longer point at the archived nougat copy.
- Added: must-fail fixtures for the php-test, phpstan and pint components: `tests/php-test-fails` carries a failing test, `tests/phpstan-fails` carries a type error, and `tests/pint-fails` is not formatted to the standard, while the clean case in `tests/fixture-app` passes all three; new checks `tests/check-php-test-fails`, `tests/check-phpstan-fails` and `tests/check-pint-fails` (sh and ps1) assert each template keeps the job line that lets the tool's exit code be the job result, then run the component's own commands from its template, in the component's own image, against both cases, and pass only when the clean case passes and the bad case fails with the expected finding. The `must-fail-php-test` and `must-fail-phpstan-pint` jobs run them in CI, in the templates' own images, and they still run locally with Docker.
- Added: the `squire-kit` component (`templates/squire-kit/template.yml`), which fails the pipeline when a Squire deploy kit drifts from the Squire release its `.squire.json` records. It installs that release from Packagist into a temporary folder (`--no-dev --no-scripts`) and runs `squire init --check` on `working_dir`; exit 0 the kit matches, 1 it drifted, 2 the check could not run. Inputs: `stage`, `job_name`, `image`, `working_dir`, `squire_version` (empty or `x.y.z`) and `allow_failure` (default `false`). It checks the recorded version, so a new Squire never turns main red by itself. Preflight's own pipeline runs it on `tests/squire-kit-fixture`, a kit written by `squire init --target=raw`. New contract test `tests/check-squire-kit` (sh and ps1). New docs page: The squire-kit component.
- Added: the preset's `waynestate/squire` rule runs `postUpgradeTasks`: it installs the new Squire into a folder under `/tmp` and runs `squire update` on the kit folder, so the merge request for a new Squire carries the refreshed kit. The renovate component gains a `squire_kit_tasks` input (boolean, default `false`) that writes the two allowed command patterns into the runner's `config.js` (`allowedCommands`); with it off the merge request bumps the version only and shows an artifact error. No shell executor is turned on. New contract test `tests/check-renovate-squire-kit` (sh and ps1) pins the commands, the patterns and 22 hostile variants they must refuse; `tests/check-renovate-review` no longer forbids `postUpgradeTasks`.
- Fixed: Renovate no longer updates files inside a Squire kit (`docker-compose.squire.yml` and `.squire/**`, outside Squire's own `templates/`). Its digest and tag bumps edited files Squire owns, which left every stack kit drifted from its recorded release and made `squire update` refuse to refresh them. Change those images in Squire's templates instead.
- Added: a must-fail fixture for the proctor component: `tests/proctor-fails` is a fake proctor that prints one blocker finding and exits 1, while the clean case in `tests/fixture-app` prints `[]` and exits 0; new check `tests/check-proctor-fails` (sh and ps1) runs both cases and keeps the template's plain redirect, so the tool's exit code stays the job result, and the contract job runs it.
- Added: the `a11y` component (`templates/a11y/template.yml`), accessibility as a gate with one include. It opens a site's pages in Chromium with Playwright and runs axe-core through `@axe-core/playwright` in light and dark mode at 320 px and 1280 px, and fails on any violation; at 320 px or less it also checks WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow, which axe-core cannot. The default tags are WCAG 2.1 AA (the ADA Title II level); `wcag22aa` adds 2.2 AA. It serves `site_dir` on a local port or checks a running site at `base_url`, takes paths or globs in `pages` (a glob that matches nothing is a configuration error, a missing page fails with HTTP 404), and writes `gl-a11y-junit.xml` (the merge request's test summary) and `gl-a11y-report.json` (every finding, plus the count axe-core left for a person to review). The image is the multi-arch Playwright image pinned by index digest; the playwright npm version comes from its tag, axe-core and @axe-core/playwright are pinned inputs, and the job fails if a different axe-core ran. `allow_failure` (default `false`) lets a site adopt it while fixing its first findings. The checker is `templates/a11y/check.mjs`, inlined in the template; new contract test `tests/check-a11y-inline` (sh and ps1) keeps the two byte for byte, and `tests/check-a11y` (sh and ps1, Docker) proves it passes a clean fixture site and fails a known-bad one with each flaw named (`tests/a11y-fixtures`). Preflight's own pipeline includes it at WCAG 2.2 AA. `renovate/default.json` bumps the two axe-core packages as one group, waiting for review. New docs page: The a11y component.
- Added: a site accessibility gate: `scripts/a11y.sh` on Linux and macOS and `scripts/a11y.ps1` on Windows run the `a11y` component's checker in Docker (same image and versions as the template, so no host browser is needed) on the front page and every docs page at WCAG 2.2 AA, in light and dark mode at 320 px and 1280 px with the reflow check, and fail on any violation; all pages pass clean. Options pick the folder, pages, tags and a report folder. The earlier copy under `tools/a11y/` is gone.
- Added: a secret-detection component (Gitleaks over the checked-out tree with `--redact`, a `gitleaks.json` report artifact uploaded even on failure, `config_path` and `allow_failure` inputs), so every stack repo gets committed-secret scanning from one include line; the first release carrying it is 0.2.0.
- Fixed: the portability component's writable-path checks now run. The `portability-run` job read `writable_paths` through `$([[ inputs.writable_paths ]])`, which GitLab does not interpolate, so the value reached the job's shell as a failing command substitution, the variable came out empty, and no `writable-*` goss check was ever appended; the line now interpolates the input as a literal string. New test `tests/check-input-interpolation` (sh and ps1) fails on any template that keeps a `$([[` form or an `inputs.` reference outside `$[[ ... ]]`.
- Fixed: the proctor and sbom jobs install the app with `--ignore-platform-reqs`. Both only read the app, yet a lock built for an older PHP or one needing gd, oci8 or ldap stopped them before PROCTOR or CycloneDX ran, so the oldest apps got no report. The sbom job also passes `--no-scripts`, so the app's Composer scripts no longer run in it. Found by the 2026-11-05 proof run; `tests/check-proctor-install-flags` (sh and ps1) now checks both lines.
- Added: a public Proof page (`docs/reference/proof.md`, under Reference): the components run against 82 Wayne State applications, what held, what the run caught in Preflight, and what it does not prove. Local checks and the README link to it.
- Added: troubleshooting entries for an install that stops on another PHP or a missing extension, a private package with no credential, and `npm ci` without a `package-lock.json`.
- Security: the front-page deploy layer moves to Symfony 7.4.23 (symfony/http-foundation and symfony/yaml advisories, including CVE-2026-118514).
- Changed: the docs theme carries the hero's sectional chart (its grid and contour rings) faintly under the top of every page, frames the overview's picture of the front page like the hero's instrument, and sets the badges in a row. Dark mode now really is the instrument panel: the kit's dark block had been winning for the page and inline code backgrounds, which left WayneUI's dark green surface everywhere; titles are panel light and the lit green is kept to links, the current page and focus.
- Changed: the docs pages wear the front page's look: its top bar and main menu (Docs marked current), B612 and B612 Mono, the cream chart page, commands on the quickstart's slab with its Copy key, callouts as the handbook's NOTE, CAUTION and WARNING boxes, tables and the pager as flight-plan forms, and the green runway footer; dark mode follows the instrument panel. New `docs/_header.html` and `docs/theme/preflight.css`, named under `theme` in `docs/docs.json`.
- Changed: the docs builder and kit are Squire's 0778fed: the theme hook, callouts, code tabs, task-list checkbox labels (fixes the axe `label` failures on the protection checklist) and a keyboard-reachable scrolling code block.
- Fixed: the contract job's Buildah pin check no longer needs git, which the mikefarah/yq image does not have; when git is missing or fails it scans regular files with find instead, skipping .git, vendor/ and node_modules/.
- Added: a Composer cache on the proctor component, keyed on composer.lock (BEST_PRACTICES 4.8); new test tests/check-proctor-cache.
- Added: every component job prints a `Preflight component <name> <version> (ref <reference>, sha <sha>)` line as its first command, so a job log says which Preflight release produced it; each template declares `spec: component: [name, version, sha, reference]`. New tests `tests/check-component-version.sh` and `tests/check-component-version.ps1`; `tests/check-spec-keys` and the template lint allow `component` under `spec:`.
- Changed: Preflight now needs GitLab 18.7 or later: `spec: component:` is generally available from 18.7, and pipeline creation fails on the unknown key on older instances.
- Added: the docs site at `site/docs/`, built from `docs/` by Squire's shared docs builder (`bin/docs-site.php`), starting with the overview page. New composer scripts: `docs` builds it, `docs:check` fails when it is stale, and `ci` now runs the check.
- Docs: component pins in the README and site examples now point at 0.1.4.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins HELMET ^0.3, PROCTOR ^0.4 and CREED ^0.1 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.0, CREED 0.1.6).
- Changed: the deploy layer sets minimum-stability to stable.
- Changed: phpstan config and memory_limit, pint config and sbom output now carry an input regex (relative paths and PHP sizes only); a value outside it stops the pipeline at creation. New test tests/check-path-input-regex.
- Added: a tag-triggered `release` job in the repository's own pipeline: pushing a protected tag creates the GitLab Release through the Releases API with curl, and the release notes carry the tag's commit SHA so consumers can pin it (BEST_PRACTICES 1.3, 1.6); new test tests/check-release-job.
- Added: a packageRule in `renovate/default.json` that restricts `quay.io/buildah/stable` to `-immutable` tags (regex versioning), so Renovate never moves a pin back to a mutable tag after Red Hat re-pushed one and garbage-collected the old digest; new test tests/check-renovate-buildah.
- Changed: the portability component's `buildah_image` default moves to the immutable tag `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb`; Red Hat re-pushed the plain version tag and garbage-collected the old digest, so pipelines pinned to the mutable tag broke. New test tests/check-buildah-pin.
- Added: an `abandoned` input on the composer-audit component (`fail`, `report` or `ignore`, default `fail`) so an app can relax how `composer audit` treats abandoned packages on purpose; the job now runs `composer audit --locked --abandoned=$[[ inputs.abandoned ]]`. New test tests/check-abandoned-input (and its `.ps1` twin) with the fixtures in tests/audit-fixtures.
- Fixed: the `portability` probe's `sigterm` check no longer fails, now and then, an app that stops at once. It checked whether the main process was still running in two steps (is its status file there, then is it a zombie), and a process reaped between the two read as running, so a clean exit could be reported as "still running 10s after SIGTERM" without any wait. It now reads the status once, takes its verdict from the same check that ended the wait, and no longer prints a stray `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` error when a process ends while the probe looks at it.

## What the components cannot force[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#what-the-components-cannot-force)

An included component is a set of ordinary jobs. The app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` is merged over them, so an app can override a job's keys, skip it with `rules`, or delete the `include:` line. Preflight makes the safe pipeline the easy one; it does not lock it. Rollcall is where skipped or weakened gates will show up. A preflight checklist only works if the pilot reads it. This page lists which jobs may be allowed to fail and the five project settings that make the gates harder to skip.

### Which jobs may be allowed to fail[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#which-jobs-may-be-allowed-to-fail)

Four components take an `allow_failure` input, all defaulting to `false`: `proctor`, `secret-detection`, `a11y` and `squire-kit`. A policy finding is a warning while an app adopts PROCTOR's rules, a secret finding while a repo allowlists its first false positives, an accessibility finding while a site fixes what the gate found on its first run, and a kit finding while a repo puts its deploy kit back to Squire's files, so each job may fail without failing the pipeline during adoption; the first three still write their reports. `composer-audit` has no such input on purpose: a known advisory must fail the pipeline. The other jobs have no `allow_failure` input either.

No template adds a global key such as `default:`, `variables:`, `workflow:` or `stages:`. `tests/check-contract.sh` (and its `.ps1` twin) fails on any top-level key in a template that is not a job named in `contract/inputs.json`, so a global key fails `composer ci`.

### Protection checklist[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#protection-checklist)

A pilot signs each line of the checklist; the plane does not sign for you. Five project settings make the gates harder to skip, and every one of them works on GitLab Community Edition:

- [ ] **Protect the default branch** and require a merge request to change it. Every change to `.gitlab-ci.yml` then gets a reviewer. (Code owner approval needs Premium, so on Community Edition the reviewer is whoever merges.)
- [ ] **Protect the release tags.** Protect `*` or the release tag pattern so only maintainers can create or move a tag. A component ref is a tag, so whoever can move it controls every pipeline that pins it.
- [ ] **Set merge request approvals to at least one** for changes to the default branch. Approvals are available on every tier, but code owner rules within them need Premium, so on Community Edition the approval rests with whoever has merge rights: rely on the merger as the reviewer.
- [ ] **Set "Minimum role to use pipeline variables" to `no_one_allowed`** unless the project needs pipeline variables. The components take inputs, which are fixed and type checked for the whole run. Self-managed GitLab defaults this setting to `maintainer`.
- [ ] **Keep secrets away from fork merge requests.** A fork's merge request pipeline runs the fork's configuration. Review a fork's `.gitlab-ci.yml` before running its pipeline, and never give it protected variables.

Note

These are project settings Preflight cannot create or check, and a read-only token drift report was considered and left out on purpose: it would trade a token for a warning, and the checklist costs nothing to keep.

## When the components run[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#when-the-components-run)

The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs. This page shows the `workflow:rules` block that runs them on every merge request and on pushes to the default branch, and why that block must live in the app's own file.

### The workflow:rules block[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#the-workflow-rules-block)

To run the components on every merge request and on pushes to the default branch, put a `workflow:rules` block in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

Note

The `workflow:rules` block must live in the app's own file. A component cannot set the pipeline's `workflow:rules` for the project that includes it, so the `merge_request_event` rule goes in the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

[![Preflight's front page: the headline Preflight, 'Every push is cleared for takeoff.', the include block for the php-test component, and the runway mark set in a heading-indicator instrument.](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/hero.jpg)](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/index.html)

## Preflight[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#preflight)

![php ^8.3](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![license MIT](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg) ![gitlab ci components: 9](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/components.svg)

**Every push is cleared for takeoff.**

Preflight is a set of GitLab CI/CD components that give every WSU app the same checks: PROCTOR, PHP tests on each supported version, Composer audit, an SBOM, Pint, PHPStan and ESLint. One include per component, pinned to a commit SHA, and the same checklist flies on every push.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Pick your path[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify the pipeline picked the component up.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its include example, inputs and defaults.

Preflight 0.1.4; GitLab components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0; MIT licensed.

Agents: fetch [https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) for a machine-readable index of this manual.

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html

## Install[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

Preflight installs as an `include:` in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`, one line per component, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### Requirements[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- GitLab 17.0 or newer. Components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0.
- Same instance only. Components work only within the same GitLab instance that hosts this project; they cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

### Install[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

All seven components

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

One component

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs, and each one lands in the `test` stage by default. Expected result: the pipeline shows the component's job, and for `php-test` that is one job per entry of `php_versions`, `8.3`, `8.4` and `8.5` by default. A green job means the check passed.

### Next steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): the same install as numbered steps with expected results.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): inputs, caching, and trying the next PHP release.
- [The a11y component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-a11y.html): the accessibility gate for a site's pages, in 0.2.0.
- [The squire-kit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html): the check that a deploy kit still matches its Squire release, in 0.2.0.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html

## Components[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#components)

Every GitLab CI component Preflight ships, with its include example, its inputs and their defaults, and the jobs and timeouts each template defines. Add one include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, then follow the per-component guide for setup. Like a real pre-flight check, the point is to find the fault on the ground, where it is cheap to fix.

Note

Components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0. They work only within the same GitLab instance that hosts this project.

![Preflight's before-takeoff checklist card. 1 PROCTOR, checked; 2 PHP tests, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 pass; 3 Composer audit, no advisories; 4 SBOM, validated; 5 Pint, clean; 6 PHPStan, no errors; 7 ESLint and Prettier, clean; 8 clearance, cleared for takeoff. Beside it the annunciator panel lights a green lamp per check, with a11y, contract and freshness marked coming soon, and lists the seven checks, all in the 0.1.4 tag.](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/checklist.svg)

The checklist, item by item, with each item's job and timeout read from `templates/`:

| # | Item | Job | Timeout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | PROCTOR | `proctor` | 30 minutes |
| 2 | PHP tests, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 | `php-test`, one job per version | 30 minutes |
| 3 | Composer audit | `composer-audit` | 30 minutes |
| 4 | SBOM | `sbom` | 30 minutes |
| 5 | Pint | `pint` | 10m |
| 6 | PHPStan | `phpstan` | 10m |
| 7 | ESLint and Prettier | `eslint` | 15m |

The `a11y`, `squire-kit` and `portability` components are the next items on the card. They ship in 0.2.0 (`portability` in its one-job form), so the picture above, drawn before them, does not show them yet:

| # | Item | Job | Timeout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | Accessibility, WCAG 2.1 AA by default | `a11y` | 30 minutes |
| 9 | Squire deploy kit matches its release | `squire-kit` | 10 minutes |
| 10 | Runs off Citadel: strict boot and six portability checks | `portability` | 30 minutes |

Every job the templates define is `interruptible: true`. Every component takes a `job_name` input whose default is the job's usual name; set it when one project includes the same component more than once.

### proctor[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#proctor)

Runs `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` and publishes the result as a GitLab Code Quality report. The job installs the app's dependencies with `composer install --no-plugins --no-scripts --ignore-platform-reqs`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run inside the job, and an app locked to an older PHP or needing an extension the image lacks still gets its report.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      proctor_command: vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `proctor` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:9cf851bc2c1b37c3e59dfd677a3c3e56d485af5a47c93f629424bb039eafcb69` | Docker image for the job. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline. |
| `proctor_command` | string | `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` | The proctor command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/proctor/template.yml`: the single job (named by `job_name`) runs in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a timeout of 30 minutes. It installs Composer with the official getcomposer.org installer, verifies the installer's SHA-384 against composer.github.io/installer.sig, and pins the installed version to `composer_version`. It then runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --no-plugins --no-scripts --ignore-platform-reqs`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run with the job's access and the app's PHP version and extensions are not required. The command's output goes through a plain redirect (not `tee`) to `gl-code-quality-report.json` at the project root, which keeps PROCTOR's exit code as the job result and gives the artifact the same path for every `working_dir`, including `.`. The report is published as a Code Quality report with `when: always`.

### php-test[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#php-test)

Runs the test command on each supported PHP version through `parallel:matrix`.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the jobs. |
| `job_name` | string | `php-test` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:${PHP_VERSION}-cli-trixie` | Docker image for the jobs. The default carries the literal `${PHP_VERSION}`, which GitLab expands in the image at job time. |
| `php_versions` | array | `["8.3", "8.4", "8.5"]` | PHP versions to test against. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `test_command` | string | `vendor/bin/phpunit` | The test command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/php-test/template.yml`: one job is created per entry in `php_versions` through `parallel:matrix`; `PHP_VERSION` becomes a CI/CD variable in each job, which the image input's default expands, and each job runs the newest patch release of its version. The default image is deliberately tag-pinned (the template points at the README section Updating image pins). Each job installs Composer the same way as proctor, runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress`, and then the test command. The jobs are `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

#### Caching[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#caching)

The jobs always cache Composer downloads in `.composer-cache/` so repeat runs do not re-download every package. The cache key depends on `composer.lock` and is prefixed with the PHP version, so a dependency change invalidates the cache and each PHP version gets its own cache. The template sets `COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR` to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.composer-cache`, keys the cache on `composer.lock` with the prefix `php-${PHP_VERSION}`, caches the path `.composer-cache/`, and uses the policy `pull-push`.

#### Try the next PHP release without breaking the pipeline[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#try-the-next-php-release-without-breaking-the-pipeline)

Include `php-test` a second time for the release that is not supported yet, name that job, and let it fail. The name is what lets your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` loosen only that job:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      php_versions: ["8.6"]
      job_name: php-test-next
      # While 8.6 only has release candidate images, name the tag: php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie
      # image: "php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie"

php-test-next:
  allow_failure: true
```

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. Drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`).

### composer-audit[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#composer-audit)

Runs `composer audit --locked` and fails on advisories.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      working_dir: .
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `composer-audit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run composer audit in, relative to the project root. |
| `abandoned` | string | `fail` | How composer audit treats abandoned packages: fail (default), report (list them, do not fail) or ignore. |

From `templates/composer-audit/template.yml`: the `composer:2` image already ships Composer, so there is no install step. The job runs `composer audit --locked` with `--abandoned` set to the `abandoned` input (`fail` by default, `report` or `ignore` to relax the abandoned check), which exits non-zero when it finds advisories, and fails the job. There is no `allow_failure` input: advisories must fail. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

#### Run it on a schedule[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#run-it-on-a-schedule)

New advisories are published after code is merged, so a green pipeline today can be stale tomorrow. Create a weekly pipeline schedule on the default branch: project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules. The component needs nothing extra; it carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled pipelines like any other. Creating the schedule is a project setting, not a file in the app's repo, and someone with Maintainer rights on the app must do it. It is the one preflight check that books its own flight time.

### sbom[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#sbom)

Generates a CycloneDX SBOM with `cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer`, validates it, and publishes it as an artifact. The plugin is installed globally, so the app's `composer.json` is never touched.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      output: sbom.cdx.json
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `sbom` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `omit_dev` | boolean | `true` | Whether to omit dev dependencies from the SBOM. |
| `output` | string | `sbom.cdx.json` | Path of the SBOM file to publish, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/sbom/template.yml`: the job runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist --no-scripts --ignore-platform-reqs` (the app's scripts never run, and its PHP version and extensions are not required), allows the plugin globally with `composer global config --no-plugins allow-plugins.cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer true`, installs `cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer:^6.2` globally, and then runs `composer CycloneDX:make-sbom --output-format=JSON --output-reproducible --validate` with `--omit=dev` added while `omit_dev` is true, writing to the `output` path. The `--validate` flag fails the job on an invalid SBOM. The SBOM file is published as an artifact with `expire_in: 30 days`. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

### pint[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#pint)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: php,style,pint

Runs the app's own [Laravel Pint](https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/pint) in test mode and fails the pipeline on style errors. The app must require `laravel/pint` as a dev dependency and ship a `pint.json` (or point `config` at its own file).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: pint.json
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `pint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `pint.json` | Path to the app's Pint config file. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run Pint in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/pint/template.yml`: the component does not install Pint itself; it runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist` and then the app's own Pint in test mode against the `config` file. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 10m.

### phpstan[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#phpstan)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: php,static-analysis,phpstan

Runs the app's own [PHPStan](https://phpstan.org/) and fails the pipeline on static analysis errors, writing a GitLab Code Quality report. The app must require `phpstan/phpstan` as a dev dependency and ship a `phpstan.neon` (or point `config` at its own file).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: phpstan.neon
      memory_limit: 1G
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `phpstan` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `phpstan.neon` | Path to the app's PHPStan config file. |
| `memory_limit` | string | `1G` | Memory limit passed to PHPStan. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run PHPStan in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/phpstan/template.yml`: the component does not install PHPStan itself; it runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist` and then the app's own PHPStan with `--no-progress --error-format=gitlab`, the `memory_limit` value and the `config` file, redirecting the output to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR/phpstan-report.json`. The report is published as a Code Quality report with `when: always`. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 10m.

### eslint[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#eslint)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: javascript,style,eslint,prettier

Runs the app's own [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) (and [Prettier](https://prettier.io/)) and fails the pipeline on lint or format errors. The app must require `@waynestate/pinstripe`, `eslint` and `prettier` as dev dependencies and ship an `eslint.config.js` (or point `eslint_args` at its own files).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      eslint_args: .
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `eslint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `node:22.13-alpine@sha256:e2b39f7b64281324929257d0f8004fb6cb4bf0fdfb9aa8cedb235a766aec31da` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the commands in, relative to the project root. |
| `eslint_args` | string | `.` | Arguments passed to eslint. |
| `prettier` | boolean | `true` | Whether to also run `prettier --check`. |

From `templates/eslint/template.yml`: the component does not install ESLint or Prettier itself; it runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --cache .npm-cache` (the cache is keyed on `package-lock.json` and stores `.npm-cache/`), then `npx --no-install eslint` with the `eslint_args` value, and, while `prettier` is true, `npx --no-install prettier --check .`. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 15m.

### secret-detection[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#secret-detection)

Version 1 · Category: Security/Secrets · Tags: security,secrets,gitleaks

Runs [Gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks) over the checked-out tree and fails the pipeline when a rule matches, with every match redacted in the job log and the `gitleaks.json` report artifact. By default it runs the built-in rules plus a path allowlist for `vendor/` and `node_modules/`, which a CI cache can restore into the checkout; point `config_path` at your own `.gitleaks.toml` to replace the default, and add the same `vendor` and `node_modules` path allowlist to your file.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/secret-detection@<full commit SHA> # 0.2.0
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `secret-detection` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.30.1@sha256:c00b6bd0aeb3071cbcb79009cb16a60dd9e0a7c60e2be9ab65d25e6bc8abbb7f` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config_path` | string | (empty) | Path to a `.gitleaks.toml` config file, relative to the project root. Empty uses the built-in rules plus a path allowlist for `vendor/` and `node_modules/`. When set, your file replaces the default, so add the same `vendor` and `node_modules` path allowlist to it. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline. |

From `templates/secret-detection/template.yml`: the single job (named by `job_name`) runs in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a timeout of 30 minutes. The job overrides the image's entrypoint with an empty value, because GitLab's Docker executor would otherwise pass the script to the gitleaks binary; the image is Alpine-based with `/bin/sh`, and the script is plain POSIX sh. The job writes the default config to `/tmp` (outside the scanned tree) unless `config_path` is set, then runs `gitleaks dir --redact --no-banner` with `--config` pointing at that file or the user's, writing a JSON report to `gitleaks.json` at the project root. The report is published as an artifact with `when: always` and `expire_in: 30 days`, so a red pipeline still shows what was found, redacted. In `dir` mode Gitleaks reads a `.gitleaksignore` at the project root without an extra flag.

### package-publish[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#package-publish)

Version 1 · Category: Release/Publishing · Tags: composer,publish,release

Publishes a semantic version tag to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry. The job runs only on tags, reads the registry first, and refuses a moved version: a version already published from this commit passes quietly, and a version published from a different commit fails the pipeline, because GitLab would otherwise overwrite it without a word. The default image ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/package-publish@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      group_id: "<your group id>"
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `deploy` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `package-publish` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. The default ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip. |
| `group_id` | string | none | Numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package. Required. |
| `read_token_variable` | string | `PACKAGE_READ_TOKEN` | Name of the masked CI variable holding a token with the `read_package_registry` scope, used to read the registry before publishing. |

Warning

Protect your release tags.

From `templates/package-publish/template.yml`: the job runs only when `$CI_COMMIT_TAG` is set. The tag must be a semantic version, `1.2.3` or `v1.2.3` with an optional pre-release, or the job fails. The package name comes from `composer.json`, the file the registry serves. The job reads the masked CI variable named by `read_token_variable`, checks that `group_id` is numeric, reads the group's Composer registry index with the token, and follows the package metadata to the version already on the manifest. A version already published at this commit passes quietly (exit 0); a version published at a different commit fails (exit 1). Publishing posts the tag to the project's Composer packages endpoint with the job token. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

### renovate[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#renovate)

Runs [Renovate](https://docs.renovatebot.com/) as a scheduled or manual job that bumps image digests, GitHub action SHAs and package versions across the group's repositories, and merges the green ones itself. Bumps of `component:` include pins are covered by the preset and wait for review. Majors open a merge request and wait for a person. See [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html) for what auto-merges and what waits.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/renovate@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      git_author: "Preflight Bot <preflight-bot@example.com>"
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_name` | string | `renovate` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `renovate/renovate:44.192.2@sha256:37960a62ba1faa9079a7c4eead9b3f4470748a64ecd207e06c09fd8858673e17` | Docker image for the job. |
| `autodiscover_filter` | string | `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE/*` | Glob limiting which projects Renovate discovers, relative to the runner project's namespace. |
| `dry_run` | string | `"null"` | Dry run mode: `null` (disabled), `lookup` or `full`. |
| `git_author` | string | none | Author of the commits and merge requests Renovate creates, in the form `Name <email>`. Required. |
| `squire_kit_tasks` | boolean | `false` | Allow the Squire kit commands of Preflight's preset (install the new `waynestate/squire` from Packagist, then `squire update` on the kit folder), so a Squire kit merge request arrives with its files refreshed. Off, the merge request bumps the version only and shows an artifact error. |

From `templates/renovate/template.yml`: the job has no `stage` input and sets no stage. It runs only on scheduled and manual pipelines (`$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"` or `"web"`). It writes its `config.js` at job time, so the `registryAliases` entry for the GitLab instance comes from the predefined `CI_SERVER_FQDN` variable; no hostname is stored in the repository, so the public mirror stays clean. It does not set `RENOVATE_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` in the job `variables:` on purpose: a self-reference such as `X: $X` arrives as literal text on GitLab 19.5 and would shadow the masked project CI/CD variables, so the job reads both tokens straight from the project. With `squire_kit_tasks` set to `true`, `config.js` also carries an `allowedCommands` list of two anchored patterns, the exact `composer create-project` and `squire update` commands of the preset's Squire rule, with the version and paths limited to safe characters; otherwise the list is empty. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 1 hour.

### portability[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#portability)

Proves the app image runs the way OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker run it, not only on Citadel (ADR-0010). One job builds the image with Buildah (vfs storage, chroot isolation: no Docker daemon, no privileged runner, no registry), boots it twice side by side as an arbitrary uid in group 0 with no capabilities, and probes it with curl. It fails unless the strict boot holds (no passwd entry for the uid, app root not writable, writable paths writable by group 0, the port variable honored, no writes outside the allowed paths) and six checks pass: `health`, `env-only`, `forwarded-headers`, `logs`, `session-hop` and `sigterm`. See [The portability component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html). No takeoff without a clean pre-flight.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/portability@<full-commit-sha> # 0.2.0
    inputs:
      env: ["APP_KEY=${PORTABILITY_APP_KEY}", "APP_URL=https://myapp.example.edu"]
      session_login_path: /_portability/login
      session_check_path: /_portability/me
```

The one-job form ships in 0.2.0; 0.1.4 carries the earlier two-job form (`portability-build`, `portability-run`). The runner must allow user namespaces, which ordinary unprivileged Docker-executor runners do.

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the portability job. |
| `job_name` | string | `portability` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb` | Buildah image the job runs in. It builds the app image and runs the probe, so it needs buildah, curl, awk and find. |
| `dockerfile` | string | `Dockerfile` | Dockerfile to build, relative to the context. |
| `context` | string | `.` | Build context, relative to the project root. |
| `build_args` | array | `[]` | Build arguments as `NAME=value`. `$NAME` and `${NAME}` in a value are replaced from the job's variables. |
| `app_root` | string | `/app` | Directory inside the image where the app lives. |
| `writable_paths` | array | `["storage", "bootstrap/cache"]` | Paths the app may write to, relative to `app_root`. Each must be writable by the uid in group 0. |
| `runtime_paths` | array | `["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/run", "/var/run"]` | Absolute paths the platform mounts as tmpfs. Writes there are allowed. |
| `port` | number | `8080` | Port the app listens on by default. The second replica gets `port + 1` through `port_env`. |
| `port_env` | string | `PORT` | Environment variable that sets the app's listen port. |
| `health_path` | string | `/up` | Path that must answer 200 for any Host, before trusted hosts, HTTPS redirects, sessions and auth. |
| `uid` | number | `100123` | Numeric uid the app runs as, with no `/etc/passwd` entry. The gid is always 0. |
| `start_command` | string | `""` | Command that starts the app, run with `sh -c`. Empty runs the image's own `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`. |
| `env` | array | `[]` | Environment for both replicas, as `NAME=value` (or `NAME` to pass the job's variable through). Keep secrets in CI/CD variables. |
| `boot_timeout` | number | `60` | Seconds each replica has to answer the health path. |
| `stop_timeout` | number | `10` | Seconds the main process has to exit after SIGTERM. |
| `probe_path` | string | `/` | Page probed with and without forged forwarded headers. |
| `identity_header` | string | `X-Forwarded-User` | Identity header a gateway would set (forged in `forwarded-headers`). |
| `session_login_path` | string | `""` | GET path that signs in a test user and sets the session cookie. Needed by `session-hop`. |
| `session_check_path` | string | `""` | Path that answers 200 only for a signed-in user. Needed by `session-hop`. |
| `logs_path` | string | `storage/logs` | Directory, relative to `app_root`, where nothing may be written. |
| `checks` | array | `["health", "env-only", "forwarded-headers", "logs", "session-hop", "sigterm"]` | The checks to run. Leave one out only on purpose; the strict boot always runs. |

The `image` default is an immutable tag (`-immutable`) pinned by digest, because the plain version tag can be re-pushed and its old digest removed.

From `templates/portability/template.yml`: one job, keyed by `job_name`, with `STORAGE_DRIVER: vfs` and `BUILDAH_ISOLATION: chroot`. It writes the inputs to a file through a quoted heredoc, writes the probe (`templates/portability/probe.sh`, inlined byte for byte because a component only ships its `template.yml`), and runs it. The probe prints one `portability: <check>: pass`, `FAIL` or `skipped` line per check and exits 1 on any failure, 2 on an input error. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

### a11y[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#a11y)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: accessibility,a11y,wcag,axe-core,playwright

Opens the app's pages in a real Chromium browser with Playwright and runs axe-core through @axe-core/playwright, in light and dark mode at 320 px and 1280 px, and fails the pipeline on any violation. The default tags are WCAG 2.1 Level AA (the ADA Title II level); add `wcag22aa` for WCAG 2.2 AA, the stack's floor. At 320 px it also checks WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow, which axe-core cannot. It writes a JUnit report and a JSON report. See [The a11y component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-a11y.html).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/a11y@<full commit SHA> # 0.2.0
    inputs:
      pages: ["index.html", "docs/**/*.html"]
      wcag_tags: ["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa", "wcag22aa"]
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `a11y` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.65.0-noble@sha256:6e3fb709361521eb27161606e6da6d2674e5e89fa16516cb37d6fdd91372273d` | Playwright image the job runs in (amd64 and arm64); its `vX.Y.Z` tag sets the playwright npm version. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline, for a site fixing its first findings. |
| `site_dir` | string | `site` | Static folder to serve, relative to the project root. Page globs expand in it. |
| `pages` | array | `["**/*.html"]` | Pages to check, relative to the site root: paths or globs. A glob must match at least one file. |
| `base_url` | string | `""` | Check a running site at this URL instead of serving `site_dir`. Empty serves `site_dir`. |
| `wcag_tags` | array | `["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa"]` | axe-core tags to run; add `wcag22aa` for WCAG 2.2 AA. |
| `color_schemes` | array | `["light", "dark"]` | Color schemes each page is checked in. |
| `widths` | array | `[320, 1280]` | Viewport widths in CSS pixels; at 320 or less the job also checks reflow. |
| `playwright_version` | string | `""` | playwright npm version. Empty reads it from the image tag. |
| `axe_core_version` | string | `4.14.0` | axe-core version; the job fails if a different one ran. |
| `axe_playwright_version` | string | `4.14.0` | @axe-core/playwright version; its axe-core range must include `axe_core_version`. |

From `templates/a11y/template.yml`: the single job (named by `job_name`) runs in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a timeout of 30 minutes. It reads the Playwright version from the image tag, installs `playwright`, `@axe-core/playwright` and `axe-core` at exact versions with `npm install --ignore-scripts` into a temporary folder outside the project, writes the inputs as JSON and the checker (inlined from `templates/a11y/check.mjs`, because a component ships only its `template.yml`), and runs it from the project root with every check at reduced motion. It writes `gl-a11y-junit.xml` (published as a JUnit report) and `gl-a11y-report.json`, kept as artifacts for 30 days with `when: always`. It exits 0 clean, 1 on a violation or a page that did not load, and 2 on a tool or configuration error. `allow_failure` is interpolated as a real YAML boolean.

### squire-kit[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#squire-kit)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: squire,deploy,drift

Installs the Squire release a deploy kit records in its `.squire.json` and runs `squire init --check` on the kit folder, so the pipeline fails when a kit file was edited, is missing or is not that release's template. It checks the recorded version, so a new Squire release never turns main red by itself; Renovate's Squire rule moves the version. See [The squire-kit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-squire-kit.html).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/squire-kit@<full commit SHA> # 0.2.0
    inputs:
      working_dir: deploy
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `squire-kit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. It needs PHP 8.3 or later and Composer. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | The kit folder: the one holding `.squire.json`, relative to the project root. |
| `squire_version` | string | `""` | Squire release to check against, `x.y.z`. Empty reads the version recorded in `.squire.json`. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline, for a repository cleaning up its first findings. |

From `templates/squire-kit/template.yml`: the single job (named by `job_name`) runs in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a timeout of 10 minutes. It installs `waynestate/squire` at the recorded version with `composer create-project --no-dev --no-scripts` into a temporary folder outside the project and runs `squire init --check --path=.` in `working_dir`. It exits 0 when the kit matches, 1 when it drifted, and 2 when the check could not run (no `.squire.json`, no released version recorded, or no such release). `allow_failure` is interpolated as a real YAML boolean.

## Shared conventions[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#shared-conventions)

This page lists the conventions the stack shares: Composer vendor, license, PHP floor and JavaScript installs. Check a package against the table when you set one up or review one, so every project starts from the same baseline.

### Conventions[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#conventions)

| Convention | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Composer vendor | `waynestate/` |
| License | MIT |
| PHP floor | `^8.3` |

Preflight itself ships these values in its `composer.json`: `waynestate/preflight` under the MIT license, requiring `php: ^8.3`.

### JavaScript installs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#javascript-installs)

JavaScript components install with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. The job carries no token beyond `CI_JOB_TOKEN` (BEST_PRACTICES.md 4.12).

### The Preflight component line[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#the-preflight-component-line)

Every Preflight job prints a `Preflight component <name> <version> (ref <reference>, sha <sha>)` line as its first command, before anything else runs. When a job misbehaves, read that line to see which Preflight release produced it: `<name>` is the component (for example `php-test`), `<version>` is the tag of the pinned release when the include is pinned by tag, `<reference>` is the ref the include points at, and `<sha>` is the commit SHA of the component template that ran. An include pinned by commit SHA shows that SHA in the line. The line needs GitLab 18.7 or later; on an older instance, pipeline creation fails on the unknown `spec: component:` key, so upgrade GitLab or pin an older Preflight tag.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#related)

- [Updating image pins](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html): why component images are digest-pinned and how to change a pin.
- [Template lint](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html): the unsafe CI patterns `composer ci` scans for before the fixture tests.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html

## Local checks[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#local-checks)

How maintainers build, test and release this project with Docker, and the Composer scripts behind the gate. The pre-flight checklist, run from your own desk: run the same gate CI runs before you push anything.

Note

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/preflight/-/blob/main/MAINTAINING.md) on the canonical repository.

### The full gate[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-full-gate)

Run the template lint and the fixture tests with Docker:

linux

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

windows

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

In PowerShell, use `${PWD}` instead of `$(pwd)`. `composer ci` is the whole gate: it runs the template lint, the fixture tests, Pint, PHPStan, the agent-ready file check and the docs site check, in that order.

### Composer scripts[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#composer-scripts)

The scripts from `composer.json`:

```json
{
    "ci": [
        "php bin/lint-templates",
        "php bin/lint-templates --test",
        "@lint",
        "@analyse",
        "@site:agent-ready-check",
        "@docs:check"
    ],
    "lint": "pint --test",
    "fix": "pint",
    "analyse": "phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G",
    "site:agent-ready": "php bin/agent-ready.php",
    "site:agent-ready-check": "php bin/agent-ready.php --check",
    "docs": "php bin/docs-site.php",
    "docs:check": "php bin/docs-site.php --check"
}
```

| Script | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ci` | the array above | The full CI gate: template lint, fixture tests, Pint, PHPStan, agent-ready files, docs site. |
| `lint` | `pint --test` | Run Pint in test mode; fails on style errors without changing files. |
| `fix` | `pint` | Run Pint and rewrite the files it finds. |
| `analyse` | `phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G` | Run PHPStan with a 1G memory limit. |
| `site:agent-ready` | `php bin/agent-ready.php` | Rewrite the Markdown twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml in `site/` (Squire's agent-ready kit). |
| `site:agent-ready-check` | `php bin/agent-ready.php --check` | Fail when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here. |
| `docs` | `php bin/docs-site.php` | Build the docs site from `docs/` into `site/docs/` (Squire's docs builder): render the pages, fill the generated command and environment reference, and stamp the current version. |
| `docs:check` | `php bin/docs-site.php --check` | Fail when the built docs site is stale or the generated command or environment reference has drifted from the CLI or source. |

### The PHP fixture app[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-php-fixture-app)

Run the PHP fixture app separately:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/tests/fixture-app:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/tests/fixture-app:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### The portability fixtures[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-portability-fixtures)

Run the portability fixtures with Docker. The check runs the component's own probe in the component's own Buildah image against `tests/portability/app`, once clean and once per flaw, and exits 0 only when the clean build passes every check and each flaw fails the check it targets. It takes about two minutes. `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` lets Buildah open the user namespace that Docker's default seccomp profile refuses; it grants no capabilities and is not `--privileged`.

linux

```sh
docker run --rm --security-opt seccomp=unconfined -v "$(pwd):/src:ro" -w /src \
  quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb \
  sh tests/check-portability.sh
```

windows

```powershell
pwsh -File tests/check-portability.ps1
```

To run some cases only, set `PORTABILITY_CASES` (for example `-e PORTABILITY_CASES="none sigterm"` on the `docker run`), or pass `-Cases none,sigterm` to the `.ps1`.

### The accessibility gate[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-accessibility-gate)

The site's pages have an accessibility gate: the `a11y` component's own checker (`templates/a11y/check.mjs`, axe-core in Playwright), run in Docker with the image and versions pinned in `templates/a11y/template.yml`, so no host browser is needed and a local run checks the same way as the pipeline. With no options it checks the front page and every docs page at WCAG 2.2 AA, in light and dark mode at 320 px and 1280 px, with the reflow check, and fails on any violation:

linux

```sh
sh scripts/a11y.sh
```

windows

```powershell
scripts\a11y.ps1
```

Options pick another folder, pages, tags, a running site or a folder for the reports: `--site=DIR --pages='["index.html"]' --tags='["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa"]' --base-url=URL --report=DIR` (PowerShell: `-Site`, `-Pages`, `-Tags`, `-BaseUrl`, `-Report`). With `--base-url=URL` (or the `A11Y_BASE_URL` environment variable) the gate checks a running site at URL instead of a folder of HTML, as the component's `base_url` input does in CI; `localhost` inside the container is the container itself, so a site on the host is reached as `host.docker.internal`.

### The accessibility fixtures[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-accessibility-fixtures)

`tests/check-a11y.sh` (and `tests/check-a11y.ps1`) prove the checker still tells a clean site from a bad one. They run the gate against `tests/a11y-fixtures` at the component's default WCAG 2.1 AA and exit 0 only when the good site passes, the bad site fails with each known flaw named (a missing `lang`, an image with no `alt`, an unlabeled input, weak contrast, a page that scrolls sideways at 320 px, and a palette that fails in dark mode only), a missing page fails with HTTP 404, and a glob that matches nothing stops with a configuration error. They need Docker; the contract job does not run them.

linux

```sh
sh tests/check-a11y.sh
```

windows

```powershell
pwsh -File tests/check-a11y.ps1
```

`tests/check-a11y-inline.sh` (and `.ps1`) checks that the heredoc in the template is a byte-for-byte copy of `templates/a11y/check.mjs`; the contract job runs it. After editing `check.mjs`, run `sh tests/check-a11y-inline.sh --write` (PowerShell: `tests\check-a11y-inline.ps1 -Write`) to copy it into the template.

### The must-fail fixtures[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-must-fail-fixtures)

`tests/check-php-test-fails.sh`, `tests/check-phpstan-fails.sh` and `tests/check-pint-fails.sh` (each with a `.ps1` twin) prove the `php-test`, `phpstan` and `pint` components still fail a bad app and pass a clean one. Each asserts its template keeps the job line it promises, then runs the component's own commands from its template, in the component's own image, against the clean case in `tests/fixture-app` and the must-fail case in its fixture (`tests/php-test-fails`, `tests/phpstan-fails`, `tests/pint-fails`), in a copy in a temp dir. They exit 0 only when the clean case passes and the bad case fails with the expected finding. The `.sh` is the payload of a container; the `.ps1` runs it with Docker. They need Docker; the contract job does not run them.

linux

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli-trixie sh tests/check-php-test-fails.sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc sh tests/check-phpstan-fails.sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc sh tests/check-pint-fails.sh
```

windows

```powershell
pwsh -File tests/check-php-test-fails.ps1
pwsh -File tests/check-phpstan-fails.ps1
pwsh -File tests/check-pint-fails.ps1
```

### The Squire kit checks[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-squire-kit-checks)

`tests/check-renovate-squire-kit.sh` (and `.ps1`) checks the preset's Squire rule: the exact two post-upgrade commands, the kit-files rule, and the `squire_kit_tasks` allow-list the renovate component writes. It compiles the commands for sample upgrades and checks that each one matches an allowed pattern, and that 22 hostile variants (shell operators, `..` paths, another package or tool, an extra flag) match none. `tests/check-squire-kit.sh` (and `.ps1`) checks the `squire-kit` template: the version it reads, the install flags, `squire init --check` and its exit codes. The contract job runs both `.sh` files; the job itself runs on `tests/squire-kit-fixture` in Preflight's own pipeline.

### Proof[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#proof)

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private site, [proof.apps.wayne.edu/preflight](https://proof.apps.wayne.edu/preflight/), behind a Wayne State employee sign-in. What was run, what held and what it caught in Preflight itself is on the public [Proof](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html) page.

### Docs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#docs)

The full documentation lives at [preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/) on the project site, built from `docs/` by Squire's docs builder. It starts with the overview page; the rest of the manual follows as the pages are written.

- `composer docs` rebuilds `site/docs/` from `docs/`; run it after editing a page.
- `composer docs:check` fails when the built site is stale; `composer ci` runs it.

The pages are committed because the deploy server serves `site/` without building. Every page links back to its Markdown, and the footer stamps the version the docs describe. Cleared for takeoff: the flight manual flies with the aircraft.

The pages wear the front page's flight deck: `docs/_header.html` is the front page's top bar and `docs/theme/preflight.css` maps its palette and B612 type onto the docs kit, with a dark mode taken from the instrument panel. `docs/docs.json` names both under `theme`. Restyle the docs in those two files, never in `site/assets/docs.css` or `bin/docs-site.php`: those are Squire's bytes.
